chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The most hateful of the names to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are Harith, Malik, and Khalid.
ai.seo_question: What are the most hated names to Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Harith, Malik, and Khalid as the most disliked names to Allah, a teaching rooted in the Shia scholarly tradition of analyzing the etymological implications of divine attributes. These names, meaning 'The Bestower of Blessings,' 'The Ruler,' and 'The Eternal,' were historically associated with pre-Islamic polytheism that attributed independent agency to created beings, thereby subtly diminishing the absolute sovereignty of Allah. This hadith underscores the theological principle of *tawhid* by cautioning against names that might imply shared or competing divine qualities.
